title: Father's trumpet and non-pressure technique
summary: The trumpet was lost after his death; she confirms his non-pressure playing, never puffing his cheeks, which he taught to his students.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: You had it for a while. And my mother, I don't know, somehow got away from her. I don't know what she did with it. But, uh, my dad was a pretty good musician.

People have told me that he was famous for not using any pressure, what they call a non-pressure system. That's right. He told me once that he could tie a string, hang the trumpet down, say from the light or someplace, and walk up to it without touching it, and play get high C on it just by touching it. That's right. Did you ever see him demonstrate anything like that?
Yes. And, uh, you never see this swell on my dad.
Never puffed out his cheeks. Never.
All from here. He used to teach that to his students, too.
Oh, did he teach many students?
Oh, yeah. He had quite a bit of students. Yeah. Quite a bit of young men. He taught, and I don't know where they are. They all, you know, gone away.
I will run into a few. I think I have talked to maybe one or two people that say they had some lessons from him. Uh-huh.
